mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: obtain the digital certificate from the Companies Office, arrange notarization of the issued form if required, then apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Authentication Unit for a New Zealand Apostille. For non-Apostille states: use the parallel Consular Legalization route, being notarization followed by MFAT legalization and then legalization at the destination embassy or consulate; never chain the two routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain the certificate, notarize if required, and request an Apostille from MFAT; Consular Legalization route for non-member states: certify the document through MFAT legalization, then present it to the destination country consular post. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing directors, secretary, local agent and banking signatories, including Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand company board of directors, with signatures verified by a New Zealand notary public or solicitor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the director signatures, then obtain an Apostille from MFAT; Consular route: notarize the resolution, obtain MFAT legalization, then obtain consular legalization from the destination jurisdiction mission. Use only the path appropriate to the receiving state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitution/Articles of Association (or statutory default rules under Companies Act 1993 if no constitution is adopted)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand company, as adopted by shareholder resolution and certified by the company secretary or founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certify the copy as an accurate record, notarize the certification, then obtain MFAT Apostille; Consular legalization route for non-member states: notarize, have MFAT legalize, and then have the destination consulate legalize. These are parallel alternatives, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand commercial bank where the company will maintain its operating account, such as ANZ Bank New Zealand, ASB Bank, Bank of New Zealand or Westpac
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: have the bank manager signature notarized and then obtain a New Zealand Apostille from MFAT; Consular route for non-member states: notarize the bank signature, obtain MFAT legalization, and then complete consular legalization at the destination embassy. Apostille and consular legalization are independent and exclusive pathways.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories and any person exercising 25% or greater ownership or control against the OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists; UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; United Kingdom and European Union consolidated sanctions lists where relevant; New Zealand autonomous sanctions designations under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and Counter-Terrorism Act 2005; and continuous adverse-media and sanctions news sweep. Politically exposed persons require enhanced due diligence including source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval, re-screening at least every 90 days, and assessment of family members and known close associates. The screening engine must produce an auditable trail of exact-match and fuzzy-match results, false-positive resolution, and risk-rating for the bank and payment processors, in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and supervisors' guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online Companies Register and Name Reservation Service (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must use Latin characters and must end with Limited or the approved statutory abbreviation Ltd. Names containing te reo Maori or other-language diacritics are acceptable if accurately transliterated into the Latin alphabet for register search. The four-tier naming doctrine is: first, a distinctive invented or arbitrary primary name; second, a mandatory statutory limited-liability suffix; third, a Latin-script phonetic transliteration where the intended commercial brand is sourced from Chinese, Japanese or another non-Latin script; and fourth, a clearance stage for prohibited and sensitive tokens, requiring third-party consent or ministerial approval before incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must first obtain the written refusal reasons from the Companies Office. The applicant may then request an internal reconsideration through the Companies Office message system, correcting any forbidden or confusing elements and attaching written consents from the relevant supervisory agency or Crown entity. If the internal reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972, or filed a fresh application using a more distinctive invented token. An existing reservation may be extended for a further 20 working days before expiry, and any third-party consent should be filed before re-submission to prevent repeated rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is technically permissible for the Companies Act registered-office and address-for-service obligation, but for a company engaged in ISIC 3240 double-shot PBT plastic injection manufacturing and e-commerce sales it is commercially and regulatory inadvisable. Inland Revenue, New Zealand Customs, local council planning authorities, product liability insurers and almost all New Zealand banks will require a physical production or storage address. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address and must not be the sole registered office where stock, machinery, employees or environmental compliance are located.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk for the first operating year is low-to-moderate, approximately 8-12%, with unannounced inspection risk increasing if: (1) GST returns are inconsistent with bank settlement volumes from Shopify Payments or Stripe; (2) customs declarations for resin and PBT imports do not match goods sold; (3) consumer-safety or trademark complaints about keycaps are lodged; (4) the registered office remains a virtual mailbox while manufacturing operations are observable; (5) the UBO register and shareholder register diverge; or (6) IRD identifies repeated refund anomalies. Potential inspectors include IRD, MBIE, local council environmental health officers, NZ Police financial crime units and, if product safety issues arise, the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12–20 (incorporation procedure), s 25 (issuance of certificate of incorporation), s 107 (registered office), ss 149–157 (director appointments and consents), ss 189–200 (share transfers and allotment records), and s 213 (company constitution adoption). Supplementary regulation: Companies (Fees) Regulations 2023; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 is not applicable to an exempt private company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), an operational business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered through the Companies Register at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 – Application for Incorporation of a Company (online lodgement authenticated via RealMe), accompanied by a Company Constitution (if deviating from the default rules in Companies Act 1993 Schedule 1), written consents to act as director, and a notice of registered office (Form NZCN2).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up share capital requirement; shares may be allotted at an infinitesimal par value (e.g. NZD 0.01 per ordinary share). No escrow account, capital deposit, bank confirmation, or certification of capital payment is required at the time of incorporation. The company may lawfully commence business and open a corporate bank account immediately upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (Adopted pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 and the Company Constitution)

RESOLVED, by the inaugural board of directors acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of a general meeting:

1. ALLOTMENT AND ISSUE OF SHARES: That the Company hereby allot and issue 100 Ordinary Shares of NZD 1.00 each to the founding shareholder [INSERT SHAREHOLDER NAME] at par, credited as fully paid in cash upon receipt of the subscription funds, and that such allotment be duly recorded in the Company's share register and notified to the Companies Office on Form NZCN8.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office of the Company be established at [INSERT REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS, NEW ZEALAND], that such address be filed with the Companies Office, and that all statutory notices and service of process be directed to that address.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: That [INSERT DIRECTOR NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the sole director of the Company, and [INSERT SECRETARY NAME OR 'DIRECTOR-AS-SECRETARY'] be and is appointed as Company Secretary, each to act in accordance with the Company's Constitution and the Companies Act 1993.

4. AUTHORITY TO COMMENCE OPERATIONS: That the Board authorises the officers to open corporate bank accounts, execute the manufacturing facility lease, procure insurance, and undertake all registrations with Inland Revenue and WorkSafe New Zealand necessary to commence the double-shot PBT plastic injection and custom mechanical keyboard keycap business.
incorporation_legal_framework.optional_electronic_incorporation_note: The entire incorporation, including name reservation, filing, payment, and instant certificate issuance, is completed online via the Companies Register electronic portal within 1–2 business hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online portal (name search and reservation module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary electronic name search on the Companies Register to verify that the proposed company name (e.g. [NAME] LIMITED) is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company, limited partnership, or registered trademark preserved on the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) register. Submit a name reservation request for the selected name plus up to two alternative names; an approved name is reserved for a statutory precedence window of 20 working days. The reservation is free of charge when made online and forms part of the incorporation workflow.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to 3 alternatives)
Name availability search results printout
IPONZ trademark clearance search (optional but recommended)
Short descriptive memorandum explaining the reason for any distinctive name component
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is declined because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing holding, the applicant may immediately submit a new name search and reserve an alternative name. If the name is rejected on public interest grounds (misleading, offensive, or implying Crown patronage), the applicant may apply in writing to the Registrar under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 for discretionary re-approval and must accompany the application with a statutory declaration clarifying the legitimate purpose of the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Incorporation Docket (Form NZCN1, Constitution, Director and Shareholder Consents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – pre-lodgement internal compliance review (no public counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form NZCN1 in accordance with the Companies Office (electronic) instructions: state the approved company name; record the registered office address (a physical New Zealand street address, not a P.O. box, and the same address may serve as the service address); nominate at least one director who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand (an individual holding a NZ residence class visa or domiciled in New Zealand); state the share structure (class and number of shares); and either elect the default constitution (Companies Act 1993, Schedule 1) or adopt a bespoke corporate constitution. Obtain a signed written consent to act as director from each proposed director (Form NZC3 – Consent to Act) and written consent from each founding shareholder to the allotment. Attach certified copies of photographic identification and proof of residential address for each director.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NZCN1 (incorporation application)
Certificate of incorporation name reservation approval (reference number)
Form NZC3 – Consent to Act as Director for each proposed director
Shareholder written consent to subscribe for shares
Bespoke constitution (if departing from statutory default rules)
Certified copy of director's passport or national ID
Proof of director's ordinary residence in New Zealand (e.g. power bill, tenancy agreement, visa approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the docket for incomplete director identification or residential address deficiencies, the applicant has 15 working days to upload the corrective documentation through the online portal. A director who fails the ordinarily-resident test shall be substituted, or the company may nominate a provisional director subject to the Registrar's approval under section 153(4). Failure to cure within the statutory window leads to rejection of the application with partial fee refund in accordance with the Companies (Fees) Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of the Incorporation Application and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register electronic filing system (authenticated via RealMe login)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register using a RealMe verified credential. Upload the completed Form NZCN1 and all supporting consents and identification files. Electronically attest that the information submitted is true and correct, pay the statutory incorporation fee of NZD 150 (approximately USD 90) using a credit card or New Zealand bank debit (POLi). Upon processing and acceptance of the application, the Companies Office automatically issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation confirming the company's legal existence, its New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and its registration date. The certificate is definitive evidence of incorporation for all subsequent registries (IRD, WorkSafe, customs, bank, and local authorities).
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation record
Completed and executed Form NZCN1
Director consent forms (NZC3)
Shareholder subscription consents
Company constitution (if adopted)
Director identity and residence evidence
Credit card / POLi payment authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of automated rejection due to data inconsistency (e.g. name mismatch, missing field), the applicant immediately receives a validation fault report; the filer corrects the flagged fields and re-lodges the application within 5 working days without losing priority. If the application is rejected a second time, the applicant may escalate to the Companies Office Business Registry Helpdesk to obtain manual assessment; any erroneous rejection may be remedied by requesting a written decision and appealing to the High Court of New Zealand under Part 5 of the Companies Act 1993, although in practice a telephonic administrative cure is achieved within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance: Adoption of the First Board Resolution, Notice of Share Allotment, and Officer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (statutory filings) and the board of directors of the newly incorporated company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, the inaugural board executes the First Board Resolution (as pro forma provided above) confirming the allotment of shares, the registered office address, and the appointment of directors and company secretary. The company must file a Notice of Share Allotment (Form NZCN8) with the Companies Office within 10 working days of the allotment, and register the particulars of each director and the company secretary (Form NZCN2 service address) within the same period. The board shall also: open a New Zealand corporate bank account using the certificate of incorporation and NZBN; pass an opening bank resolution designating authorised signatories; and print and issue physical share certificates to the founding shareholder. A separate resolution shall adopt a corporate seal if the constitution requires one.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (original executed copy)
Form NZCN8 – Notice of Share Allotment
Form NZCN2 – Director and Registered Office Particulars
Share register for the new company
Bank account opening application and board resolution for signatories
Share certificates (physical or electronic)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Form NZCN8 allotment notice is filed after the 10-working-day deadline, a late filing penalty of NZD 100 applies; the company may apply to the Companies Office for remission under section 388 of the Companies Act 1993 on the grounds of inadvertence and immediate compliance. Any defect in director appointments (e.g. vacancies, lack of ordinary residence) is cured by lodging Form NZCN2 with revised particulars and, where necessary, passing a board resolution to appoint a replacement director with valid consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Business Registrations with Inland Revenue (IRD Number, GST, PAYE, and EMA/E-Invoicing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD) – myIR secure online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to Inland Revenue for a company IRD number using the certificate of incorporation and NZBN; the IRD number is allocated within 5 working days for a fully electronic application. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the company's expected annual turnover of taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeds NZD 60,000 (for the planned e-commerce model, registration is strongly recommended to reclaim input VAT on capital equipment and lease expenditure). Elect a standard balance date of 31 March (mandatory for New Zealand income tax unless a 12-month exemption applies). Register as an employer (PAYE) if the company will hire staff, and subscribe to the Employment New Zealand information service. Opt-in to PEPPOL e-invoicing to enable frictionless B2B transactions with the payment rails Shopify Payments and Stripe. Obtain a Customs Client Code (if importing raw PBT polymer pellets from overseas suppliers).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN certificate
Directors' individual IRD numbers
Registered office address and service address
Projected GST turnover declaration
Bank account details for IRD refunds
Customs client code application form (for import/export)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is delayed due to director identity verification, the company must upload additional certified identity documentation via myIR and obtain a verified RealMe credential for the director. Any prospective GST registration after trading has commenced is cured by applying for provisional GST registration and retrospectively collecting GST on all taxable supplies from the operative date; IRD will assess penalties only for demonstrable wilful default, and an administrative remission is available for first offenders under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Premises, Building, Fire, and Workplace Safety Clearances for the Plastic Injection Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Territorial Authority (District/City Council building and planning department), Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure an industrial zoned leasehold or freehold premises suitable for plastic injection moulding. Engage a licensed building surveyor to verify that the premises possess a current Compliance Schedule and Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) under the Building Act 2004 (including means of escape from fire, disabled access, seismic strengthening compliance to NZS 1170.5, and structural load capacity for injection-moulding machines). Submit the premises layout plan to the Territorial Authority to confirm the manufacturing activity constitutes a Permitted Activity under the operative District Plan (light industrial use). With FENZ, register a Fire Evacuation Scheme if more than 10 persons are employed in the building or high-risk hazardous substances are stored. With WorkSafe New Zealand, ensure the company, as a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU), implements a written Health and Safety at Work (HSW) policy, a hazard register, and machine-safety procedures (guards, interlocks, emergency stops) compliant with AS/NZS 4024.1. Register the automated injection-moulding machinery with the local electrical inspectorate (low voltage and pressure safety) and obtain a Certificate of Verification from an independent electrical inspector.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Title or registered lease for the industrial premises
Building Warrant of Fitness and Compliance Schedule
Territorial Authority planning confirmation (Permitted Activity certificate or letters of compliance)
FENZ Fire Evacuation Scheme approval (if applicable)
WorkSafe NZ HSW policy and hazard register
AS/NZS 4024.1 machinery risk assessment and compliance report
Electrical Certificate of Verification for high-voltage or three-phase equipment
Evidence of waste disposal contract (plastic scrap recycle) under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a BWoF inspection reveals non-compliant fire or structural elements, the company may apply for a Certificate of Acceptance (s 96 Building Act 2004) to legalise existing building work and simultaneously carry out remedial upgrades. For planning failures, the company may lodge a resource consent application for a restricted discretionary activity with the Territorial Authority to regularise the manufacturing use, or relocate to a compliant industrial subzone. Any FENZ rejection of the Fire Evacuation Scheme is cured by amending the evacuation procedures and resubmitting; repeated non-compliance may require hiring a specialist fire safety consultant and obtaining an operational licence under the FENZ Compliance Hub.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (health, safety, machinery guarding, and hazardous substance certification) jointly with the Local Territorial Authority (District/City Council building and planning control) and the Electricity Safety Authority for electrical installations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating Clearance and Certificate of Compliance for a Plastic Injection Moulding Facility (issued under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and the Building Act 2004); if the facility is classified as a lower-risk workplace, WorkSafe NZ registration is completed via the 'Safe Work' notification system rather than a separate plant-specific permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand for nationally significant proposals with residual coordination by the Local Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA) for all district-scale industrial discharges
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration/Permitted Activity (Low Environmental Risk). The double-shot PBT thermoplastic injection molding of keyboard keycaps, using pre-coloured polymer pellets, is a light-manufacturing operation of limited scale; under the RMA and the applicable District Plan, such activity is typically a Permitted Activity requiring no formal resource consent or full EIA Report, provided that noise levels remain below 50 dBA L10 at the site boundary, all cooling water is recirculated in a closed-loop system with no off-site discharge, and solid plastic scrap is segregated for recycling. A Minor Resource Consent (restricted discretionary activity) is only triggered where the site processes more than 5 tonnes of polymer per month, or where an air discharge baseline of 1 mg/m³ for total suspended particulates is exceeded, in which case a discharge-to-air permit must be obtained from the Territorial Authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater/Trade Waste: any negligible cooling blowdown must meet the local Trade Waste Bylaw limits of pH 5.5–10.0, total suspended solids (TSS) < 100 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) < 300 mg/L, and hydrocarbons < 15 mg/L; the facility must apply for a Trade Waste Consent if blowdown exceeds 2 m³/day. Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) emitted from molten PBT resin during injection cycles must remain below the workplace exposure standard of 50 mg/m³ time-weighted average (TWA) as per AS/NZS 3580 ambient air methods; no visible plume or odour may cross the boundary. Noise: maximum instantaneous Lmax of 75 dBA at the boundary and L10 not exceeding 50 dBA during day hours; compliance with NZS 6801:2008 and NZS 6802:2008 measurement protocols is mandatory. Waste: all sprue, reject mouldings, and runner scrap must be internally granulated and recycled; zero landfill disposal of PBT is the operational standard; monthly waste transfer certificates are required. Hazardous substances (cleaning solvents, mould release agents) must be stored in a compliant secondary-containment cabinet and comply with the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Property Controls) Regulations 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) approval of the Fire Evacuation Scheme for the premises, annual evacuation drill, maintenance of fire extinguishers (AS 2444) and fire hoses, pressurised-lobby smoke control where required for multi-level buildings, and a lift emergency operation fixture log. Structural Load Clearance: appointment of a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) to verify the mezzanine and machine-floor load capacity (NZS 1170.5 seismic rating) for each injection moulding machine (max 500 kN closing force); issuance of a structural certificate for floor vibration and static live load; the building must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) including compliance schedule. Occupational Clearance: WorkSafe NZ notification as a PCBU under Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, a documented HSW policy and risk register, machine guarding and interlocking to AS/NZS 4024.1, emergency stop circuit certification, crowd control and PPE (safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, hearing protection) programme, and a 6-monthly machinery safety audit by an independent WorkSafe-accredited assessor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) Te Tari Taake, Wellington, New Zealand; primary official portal is myIR at www.ird.govt.nz. Export declaration and customs administration is performed by the New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Ārai o Aotearoa) through the Trade Single Window. IRD is the sole national competent authority for income tax, GST, PAYE, and international tax rules; NZ Customs is the border enforcement counterpart for export substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop:
STEP 1 - Corporate registration: A foreign entity carrying on business in New Zealand must register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). An NZ-resident limited company (NZ_LTD) is incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 and receives its NZBN, Companies Register number, and IRD number through the integrated incorporation filing. 
STEP 2 - IRD number application: Non-resident and overseas-incorporated companies apply for an IRD number on form IR742 via myIR or paper, submitting certified certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and 25%+ shareholder identity details, the NZBN or overseas registration number, and evidence of a New Zealand resident agent for service of process. Resident NZ limited companies receive the IRD number automatically upon incorporation or may apply online through myIR. 
STEP 3 - GST registration: After IRD number issuance, register for GST in myIR; compulsory registration arises when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period. Exporters may voluntarily register to recover input credits; non-resident suppliers may appoint a GST representative. 
STEP 4 - Employer schemes: If employees are engaged, register for PAYE, KiwiSaver, and ACC through myIR. 
STEP 5 - Customs exporter registration: Register with NZ Customs for a Client Code via the Trade Single Window to lodge electronic export entries; obtain tariff classification advice for polymer keycaps (commonly HS 3926.90 or as computer peripheral parts) and confirm no export licensing restrictions apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: An NZ limited company is a separate taxable legal person under the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to a flat 28% corporate income tax rate with full dividend imputation. It is not a pass-through entity by default. A tax-resident NZ company is taxed on worldwide income, subject to foreign dividend exemptions and active CFC/foreign branch relief; a non-resident company is taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income (territorial nexus). No tax-exempt zone status applies to this entity or jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections and regimes include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election - a closely held NZ company with five or fewer eligible owners may elect under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 to be treated as a transparent pass-through entity (form IR745). (2) Imputation Credit Account (ICA) election - a company may elect to maintain an ICA and attach imputation credits to shareholder dividends. (3) Loss offset election - wholly-owned group companies may elect to transfer losses within the group. (4) GST group registration election - related companies may elect under s 55 of the GST Act 1985 to file a consolidated GST return and disregard inter-company supplies. (5) GST apportionment and mixed-use asset elections under s 91A. (6) Controlled foreign company reporting elections, including branch-equivalent and active business relief provisions. New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification regime; hybrid and branch mismatch rules under subparts FH and FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 deny deductions for unintended hybrid outcomes, and no elective hybrid blocker is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - a broad-based, destination-principle, full-input-credit consumption tax functionally equivalent to VAT, imposed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and administered by Inland Revenue. It is the sole national indirect tax in New Zealand; there is no separate sales tax, use tax, or state-level GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period triggers mandatory GST registration (s 51 GST Act 1985). Non-resident offshore suppliers of remote services and low-value goods (goods valued under NZD 1,000) to New Zealand-resident consumers must also register once their New Zealand-resident turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 per annum (ss 54C-54D). Exporters may register voluntarily below the threshold to recover input tax; the threshold is calculated exclusive of GST using a 12-month lookback and reasonable expectation look-forward test.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance regime, mandatory digital stamping, continuous transaction controls, or API-based tax clearance. E-invoicing is voluntary and is promoted through the New Zealand e-Invoicing framework based on Peppol standards (OASIS UBL 2.1 and PINT). Since 1 April 2022 central government agencies accept Peppol e-invoices for B2G transactions. All GST-registered persons must file returns electronically via myIR (GST101 or GST101A), selecting monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing periods. Tax invoice compliance under s 24 of the GST Act 1985 requires a tax invoice to be issued within 28 days of the time of supply for taxable supplies above NZD 50; simplified tax invoices are available for supplies below NZD 1,000 exclusive of GST; buyer-created tax invoices are permitted only with IRD approval; all e-invoice and tax records must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: A supply of goods is zero-rated under s 11(1)(a)-(b) of the GST Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand before the earlier of the time of supply or the 28th day after the time of supply, or where goods are supplied to a non-resident and exported before the 28th day, provided the goods are not subsequently reimported or diverted into the New Zealand domestic market. For NZ_LTD's custom mechanical keyboard keycap business (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 334118), zero-rating applies to injection-moulded double-shot PBT keycaps exported directly to overseas distributors, retailers, and end customers when the company holds valid customs export entries, transport documents, and payment remittance evidence. Services: Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under s 11(1)(d) where the non-resident recipient is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and the services are not directly connected to New Zealand land or goods situated in New Zealand; remote and digital services supplied to non-residents (design, prototyping, SaaS, technical support) are zero-rated under s 11(1)(mc) and related provisions. The exporter must establish the non-resident status of the recipient, the foreign performance or export of goods, and the absence of use in New Zealand. Input tax attributable to zero-rated export supplies is fully creditable, and a cash refund is payable when the registered exporter is in a net input-tax position.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - electronic export entry lodged with New Zealand Customs via the Trade Single Window using the registered exporter Client Code
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure of the goods from New Zealand to the overseas destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/foreign-exchange confirmation (SWIFT MT103 or NZ bank foreign-currency receipt) evidencing receipt of export sale proceeds
Commercial Invoice expressly stating 'Zero-rated for GST (export)' and detailing the goods, value, HS tariff classification, and overseas consignee
Packing List and transport/container manifest including container or seal number where applicable
Certificate of Origin or supplier's declaration where preferential tariff or treaty-based evidentiary support is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Audit scrutiny: Inland Revenue cross-matches GST returns with NZ Customs export entries, shipping and airfreight manifests, bank and payment-service-provider FX flows, and commercial documentation; IRD may issue formal information requests under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and conduct site visits to verify the physical export and the existence of the overseas customer. If zero-rating is disallowed, the supply is reassessed at 15% GST with use-of-money interest (UOMI) running from the original return due date. Civil shortfall penalties under Part IX of the Tax Administration Act 1994 are: 20% of the tax shortfall for lack of reasonable care; 10% for an unacceptable tax position; 50% for an abusive tax position; and 100% for evasion or a similar act, with possible escalation for repeated conduct. The standard four-year reassessment window is extended without limitation where fraud or evasion is involved. Criminal liability: knowingly making a false export declaration to Inland Revenue or NZ Customs is prosecutable under s 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Customs and Excise Act 2018, exposing a body corporate to fines up to NZD 250,000 and responsible individuals to imprisonment for up to five years; directors and officers may be held personally liable. Repayment of the clawed-back GST does not discharge criminal liability, and successful prosecution may also result in forfeiture of goods and director disqualification orders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account under an open and liberalised regime. New Zealand maintains no material exchange controls, no prior approval requirements for foreign investment in the manufacturing sector, and no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, branch remittances, interest, royalties, or loan repayments. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, portfolio flows, and offshore borrowing, are freely permitted subject only to general anti-money laundering obligations, Overseas Investment Act screening for significant business assets or sensitive land, and balance-of-payments reporting requirements to the Reserve Bank. For a custom mechanical keyboard keycap manufacturer (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 334118), no sector-specific FX licence is required, and profit remittance to non-resident shareholders may be executed freely via commercial banks in NZD or any freely convertible currency without exchange control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no timeline for repatriation of export receipts. Exporters may retain export earnings in foreign currency accounts at registered New Zealand banks or offshore accounts, and may convert to NZD at freely negotiated market rates. This creates zero cash-flow friction for the NZ Ltd entity's global e-commerce sales routed through Shopify Payments and Stripe, and no compliance calendar or conversion obligation is triggered for receipts from the sale of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Capital Escrow Account / Business Operational Account
Business Transactional Account / NZD and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for fully offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business) acting as the primary treasury anchor. These providers do not hold a New Zealand banking licence under the Reserve Bank deposit-taking framework and generally cannot offer ESAS settlement access, domestic direct debit mandates, or full NZD clearing. Some, such as Wise, operate with a New Zealand financial service provider registration and can offer NZD receipt routes using partner banks, which supports low-value e-commerce disbursements only. For the target entity, the legally robust architecture is a hybrid: a tier-1 New Zealand bank account for all settlement-grade liquidity and capital transactions, supplemented by an FMA-registered authorised payment provider for cross-border currency conversion and vendor payments in jurisdictions where the bank's correspondent network is less efficient.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted by New Zealand tier-1 banks for both local and non-resident directors of a registered New Zealand company, subject to digital identity verification (e.g., a New Zealand verified identity service, authenticated passport, proof of residential address) and a telephonic or video interview with the AML/CFT compliance team. A physical in-person appearance is ordinarily waived where the company has a registered office and agent in New Zealand, beneficial ownership is transparent, and the business plan reflects verifiable e-commerce operations. However, banks reserve discretion to require a physical interview where monthly expected turnover exceeds NZD 50,000, where a director is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, or where the source of funds is not fully traceable. For a standard NZ Ltd with non-resident shareholder-directors, remote opening is achievable with a certified copy of the director's passport, a Certificate of Incorporation, and a registered agent attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious beneficial ownership opacity (e.g., nominee shareholders or a layered offshore holding structure) leading the bank to query economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified share register, ultimate beneficial owner declaration with passport and proof of residential address, notarised trust deed summary if a trust is in the chain, entity structure chart, New Zealand IRD tax residency evidence for all shareholders, and a board resolution confirming the legitimate capital formation of the NZ Ltd.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds mismatch risk for a large shareholder loan injection that exceeds the operating cash-flow requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-compliant shareholder loan agreement, bank statements tracing funds from the lending entity's account, transaction purpose code declaration (e.g., BOP intercompany loan classification), detailed financial projections substantiating the working capital use, and confirmation that no exchange control approval is required in New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty jurisdiction screening flags for suppliers or customers in higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., cross-border resin suppliers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent compliance screening reports (e.g., World-Check), corroborating trade documentation (purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations), due diligence questionnaires from the counterparty, and an explanatory memorandum to the bank's sanctions and international business team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from cryptocurrency exchange transactions raises AML suspicion regarding the original source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of fiat-to-cryptocurrency conversion from a regulated exchange, complete KYC records on the exchange, source of wealth substantiation (e.g., employment contracts, asset sale agreements), transaction chain for each capital deposit, and a legal opinion confirming the capital structure's lawful provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated business activity and expected card-not-present e-commerce settlement flows for custom mechanical keyboard keycaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Declared ISIC 3240 / NAICS 334118 classification, Shopify and Stripe sales channel agreements, product catalogue, third-party fulfilment records demonstrating physical goods delivery, chargeback statistics, and a business plan aligning anticipated payout volumes with current and projected order forecasts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a non-resident shareholder capital injection into the NZ Ltd: (a) execute a SWIFT MT103 wire from the investor's offshore bank to the receiving New Zealand bank's SWIFT BIC using the beneficiary's BIC and NZD-denominated account number; (b) in the remittance advice, cite the correct Reserve Bank of New Zealand balance-of-payments purpose code – 'Direct Investment: Equity Capital' (BOP code 3410) for share subscription, or 'Intercompany Lending' (BOP code 3440) for shareholder loans; (c) include the NZ company's IRD number and the bank-assigned Customer Owner Identification Number (COIN) as remittance references; (d) for investment amounts exceeding the Overseas Investment Act screening threshold (currently NZD 100 million for significant business assets, or for sensitive land transactions), file an Overseas Investment Office consent application before remittance; for a low-capital custom keycap manufacturer, no OIO consent is ordinarily required; (e) provide the bank with a certified share register, signed subscription agreement, board resolution, and a declaration that the funds originate from a legitimate commercial source. The NZD is freely convertible, so the inward remittance will be credited immediately in NZD, or in the original currency if a foreign-currency account is used, with no surrender or escrow period.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the procurement of PBT resin, double-shot mould tooling, and injection-moulding equipment may be executed via: (a) standard SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers through all tier-1 New Zealand banks, using the 'Goods Trade – Import of Raw Materials' BOP classification (code 4100); (b) commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700 form) opened by the New Zealand bank in favour of resin suppliers or mould manufacturers in China, Taiwan, or Japan, with sight or usance tenor (typically D/P 120 days) compliant with UCP 600 and Incoterms 2020 rules; (c) e-commerce settlement flows from Shopify Payments and Stripe are captured into the NZD operational account via the Reserve Bank's real-time gross settlement system (ESAS – Exchange Settlement Account System), with standard T+1 payout cycles; (d) high-volume disbursements to suppliers in Asia may be batched through the bank's online payments portal using SWIFT MT101 instructions to optimise FX conversion rates; and (e) all disbursements over NZD 50,000 are subject to enhanced counterparty due diligence in line with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) for USD/NZD, EUR/NZD, and CNH/NZD with tenors of up to 12 months to fix accounts receivable and payable conversion rates.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore for currencies for which no deliverable NZD market exists within New Zealand, used exclusively to hedge emerging-market procurement exposures such as CNY/NDF positions.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge foreign-currency-denominated debt or capital injections and align interest cash flows with the NZD functional currency.
Zero-cost collars and vanilla FX options (call/put structures) providing asymmetric downside protection for highly variable e-commerce settlement volumes.
FX swaps (spot-to-forward and forward-to-forward) executed through the tier-1 bank's treasury desk to efficiently roll over foreign-currency working capital positions without residual market risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation (confirmation date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar issues a default notice; continued non-compliance leads to strike-off from the Companies Register. Maximum fine of NZD 10,000 may be imposed on the company or directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 7 July following a standard 31 March financial year end, or 7 months after an approved non-standard balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 250 if filed within two months after due date, increasing to NZD 500 for further delay; use-of-money interest applies to any unpaid tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to large companies, defined as those with total assets exceeding NZD 30 million or annual revenue exceeding NZD 15 million in the two most recent consecutive accounting periods. Public issuers, overseas companies, and other entities required under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 are also audited. Other private companies may dispense with audit by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP established by the External Reporting Board; for-profit entities apply NZ IFRS, with eligible entities able to adopt NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) or simplified SME reporting standards as permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO register. The annual confirmation process requires directors to verify that the registered shareholders and directors listed on the Companies Register are current and accurate. Any transfer of shares during the year must be filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the transfer.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand grants no statutory corporate tax holidays. Effective-rate reductions arise from the Research and Development Tax Incentive (a 15% credit on qualifying R&D expenditure, capped at NZ$120,000,000 per group per annum), immediate expensing of low-value assets (NZ$5,000 or less), simplified depreciation for manufacturing plant and injection-mould tooling, and the imputation credit system which attaches a 28% credit to distributions so that fully imputed dividends bear no further corporate-level tax. The statutory loss carryforward allowance is preserved under the shareholder-continuity and business-continuity ownership tests.
